How I work

A simple routine that keeps you informed and in control of what goes on your page.

  1. Discovery call

    We talk about your stay, your guests and what you want your page to do.

  2. Page review and plan

    I review your page and set a simple content plan you can approve.

  3. Create

    I make the graphics, captions and reels. You approve before anything is posted.

  4. Post and reply

    I schedule posts and help answer guest messages during agreed hours.

  5. Review and adjust

    Each month you get a short report on what worked, and we adjust the plan.

About me

I’m a Computer Engineering graduate who works as a social media marketer for small pension houses and beach/pool resorts.

I have helped with a local pension house and a beach and pool resort, so I understand what guests ask and what owners need. My background in data analysis and virtual assistance makes me organized, detail-focused and comfortable with digital tools.

My approach is simple: keep your page clear, keep it active and make booking easy. I plan the content, make the graphics, reply to guests and track what works, so you can focus on running your stay.

Common questions

Quick answers for owners who are thinking about working with me.

What do you need from me to start?

Your page name, a few photos of your rooms and facilities, your rates and house rules, and one person I can message for quick questions. I’ll send a simple checklist after the discovery call.

Do you need my Facebook password?

No. I ask you to give me access through your page’s roles and permissions, so you stay the owner and can remove my access any time.

Who approves the posts?

You do. Nothing goes live until you approve it, unless we agree on a standing routine for simple posts.

Can I change my package later?

Yes. You can move up or down at the start of any month as your needs change.

Do you promise more bookings?

No one can honestly promise that. I focus on what I can control: a clear, active page with accurate details, quick replies and a monthly report so you can see what is working.
